implementation_notes: crossbeam-queue supplies both shapes of the classic structure: ArrayQueue is a bounded MPMC ring (Vyukov's bounded MPMC algorithm - per-slot stamps and CAS on cache-padded head/tail indices), SegQueue an unbounded MPMC queue that allocates segments on demand and advances atomic head/tail positions with a backoff loop. Both are safe without a manual reclamation scheme because ownership (T: Send) decides exactly when a popped value is dropped, and both are usable in no_std with alloc. std::sync::mpsc remains the first choice when there is one consumer: channel() is unbounded, sync_channel(n) is bounded and blocking, and the API models disconnection, which the MPMC queues do not. The classic structure is replaced by the crate rather than written out; hand-rolling over AtomicPtr still needs an epoch/hazard scheme to know when a popped node may be freed.
pitfalls: pop() returning None means empty, not disconnected: unlike mpsc there is no channel-closed signal, so shutdown needs a sentinel or an AtomicBool.
Empty means empty right now - a spin loop around pop() burns a core; yield, park, or pair the queue with a Condvar when consumers must sleep.
ArrayQueue::push returns Err(value) when full and SegQueue::len() is an approximate traversal; neither is a synchronisation point.
